subject: Comparing the spatial effects of two models

messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Comparing the spatial effects of two models
parts:
hello,

I have a question about comparing the spatial effects of two models using r-inla. Assuming I have two models: Model 1 and Model 2. Where Model  1 is a survival model with the formula (adopted from Martine, Akerkar & Rue (2011):

f1 = inla.surv(time, event)∼ PM+ f(ID, model="iid", param=c(1, 1))

and Model 2 is expressed as 

f1 = inla.surv(time, event)∼ PM+ age + edu + inc + f(ID, model="iid", param=c(1, 1))

where ID is an index for spatial units.

Is there a way to compare the spatial effects from the two models in terms of change in the spatial risk? Can I just do such a comparison by looking at the differences in the log hazards for ID in the two models (e.g. Model 1 - Model 2)?

Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Comparing the spatial effects of two models
parts:
Maybe you want to compare DIC or WAIC, if you're up to a model
comparison. Otherwise, if you're after the chance in the risk, you have
to check how to risk for the two fits differ.
